successors.name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
successors.text: Hunza and Nagar, which 'acceded to Pakistan' in November 1947

ledger.x: c. 1200: the principality of Hunza is established. 'Hunza was an independent principality, established in around 1200'; infobox 'Established: c. 1200'. The page gives the year loosely and no boundary; the disc is the infobox's 10,000 km2.

c. 1300: Nagar appears beside Hunza. 'Nagar was established in the 14th century and existed as an autonomous principality'; the pair is drawn as one state. The page says the early rulers' details are uncertain and the first definite dates are from 1839.
November 1947: Hunza and Nagar accede to Pakistan.

wars.name: Hunza-Nagar Campaign
wars.outcome: British victory: Hunza captured 22 December and the Baltit Fort and Nagar on 23 December 1891; Nazim Khan and Zafar Khan installed as the new rulers of Hunza and Nagar; the column was back in Gilgit on 11 January 1892.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier of either state or a line between them; one 70 km disc stands for both.
